title: Introduction to Lumen Clocks

sections.title: The Lumen Circle
sections.teaches: Defining the structure of a lumen clock with 7 marks.
sections.visual: A circle appears with 7 evenly spaced tick marks labeled 0 through 6. The numbers are placed clockwise starting from the top (12 o'clock position). A hand points to mark 0 initially.
sections.narration: Welcome to the Lumen clock, a unique timekeeping device based on modulo 7 arithmetic. It features exactly seven marks, numbered 0 to 6, arranged in a circle.

sections.title: The Two-Mark Rule
sections.teaches: Explaining the movement rule: one tick = +2 marks.
sections.visual: An animated hand starts at mark 0. It jumps forward two positions to mark 2, then another two to mark 4. Arrows indicate the direction of movement. The text '+2' appears briefly above each jump.
sections.narration: In a lumen clock, one tick advances the hand by exactly two marks. This means we skip every other number as we move clockwise around the circle.

sections.title: Wrapping Around
sections.teaches: Demonstrating the wrap-around mechanic using the worked example.
sections.visual: The hand starts at mark 3. It jumps to mark 5, then jumps past mark 6 and lands on mark 0. A curved arrow illustrates the wrap from 6 back to 0. Text '3 → 5 → 0' appears.
sections.narration: When the hand passes mark 6, it wraps around to 0. For example, starting at 3, two ticks take us to 5, and the next tick lands us on 0.

sections.title: The Full Cycle
sections.teaches: Showing that 7 ticks return the hand to start and visit all marks.
sections.visual: A rapid sequence shows the hand visiting every mark: 0→2→4→6→1→3→5→0. After returning to 0, a checkmark appears next to each visited number to show they were all covered.
sections.narration: After exactly seven ticks, the hand returns to its starting position. Crucially, this process ensures that every single mark from 0 to 6 is visited before the cycle repeats.

source: A lumen clock has 7 marks, 0 to 6, around a circle. One lumen tick moves the hand forward by 2 marks, wrapping past 6 back to 0. Rules: (1) after 7 ticks the hand is back where it started. (2) The hand visits every mark before it returns. Worked example: from mark 3, two ticks go 3 → 5 → 0.
